addressGoes: Meta's app dashboard, in the Instagram product's webhook settings, with INSTAGRAM_VERIFY_TOKEN as the verify token

settings.description: The token Meta sends back when it checks your server's address: any text of your own, entered as the webhook's verify token.

why.maxTextLength: Instagram takes 1,000 bytes of text in a message, counted as UTF-8, and the adapter cuts a longer one short and says nothing (INSTAGRAM_MESSAGE_BYTE_LIMIT, truncateUtf8). A reply is split by its characters, and a character is up to 3 bytes: 333 characters are within 1,000 bytes whatever they are. 1,000 would lose the end of any part that isn't plain ASCII (half of one in Cyrillic).
why.addressGoes: The adapter has no call that gives Instagram the address: a person enters it, and the verify token with it, on Meta's page. Instagram then sends a GET with that token, which the adapter answers.
why.plainText: Instagram shows text as it is typed. The adapter flattens Markdown to plain text itself, and in doing so drops a list's numbers and a link's address. Text sent as a string is left as it is.
why.settings: The verify token is the caller's own choice: Meta is given it with the address, and sends it back in the GET it checks the address with (hub.verify_token), which the adapter compares with this setting.
